sources.title: NEA Big Read: Beloved
sources.note: Connects nonlinear memory, haunting and narrative agency; records contested institutional recognition before the Pulitzer. Supports sustained rereading beyond a simple historical plot.
sources.limits: Guide, not an independent ranking. Biographical date inconsistencies are excluded from catalog verification.

sources.title: Moby, without the Dicks
sources.author: Jenny Diski
sources.note: Defends digression and verbal texture against abridgment: apparent obstacles can constitute the novel’s reading reward. Searls’s extracted omissions are a separate project.
sources.limits: Short intervention about abridgment, not a comprehensive critical study; shares LRB ownership with other consulted articles.

sources.title: The Cacophonous Miracle of The Brothers Karamazov
sources.author: Jennifer Wilson
sources.note: Finds formal coherence in conflicting voices and shared guilt; praises Katz’s dialogue while confronting the author’s exclusionary nationalism.
sources.limits: One interpretation; translation praise is not consensus.

sources.title: To arms!
sources.author: Patrick Parrinder
sources.note: Reads contradictory ambitions through capitalism, censorship and blocked political agency. Notes the revised Welsh translation’s restored material and appendix; questions include antisemitism and international neglect.
sources.location: Review paragraphs on narrative, censorship, politics and reception
sources.limits: Reviews 1996 edition, not direct verification of every feature of 2011 reissue. Historical reception claims are time-specific.
